actor: mk — solo gardener of a ~98-project estate, directing agents from Aleph's Home
trigger: An agent reaches a fork it should not choose alone. Instead of asking in chat and idling, it files a decision owed and moves on; later mk opens Home and sees the decision waiting on the rail.

steps.step: The asker files the decision in one call: the question, two to four options, its recommendation, the project, its own thread id, and a continuation on every option — a command, a brief, needs-context, or ruling-only. It then carries on with other work, or ends its turn; nothing waits on the answer unless it chose needs-context
build_surface: Clavain decision-filing helper + shared agent guidance (new)
hub-tracker decision bead with continuation fields (new)
continuation command frozen by hash at filing (new)
filing helper requires a continuation kind on every option; ruling-only is explicit (new)

steps.step: mk opens Home and reads the catch-up first; the decision sits on the rail with the others owed, oldest first, tagged with its project; a decision gone stale (a newer ruling or later work touching the same ground) is marked stale rather than hidden

mk opens one decision and sees everything needed to answer without visiting the thread: the question, each option with its exact command or brief, the recommendation and why, and a link to the asking thread if they want more
build_surface: bb thread link (@thread) from the bead's asking_thread

steps.step: mk picks an option. The pick is the whole approval, but first the continuation is re-checked: its hash and preconditions still hold, or the pick becomes a re-ask. Then the frozen command runs, a brief starts a fresh small thread, needs-context queues a wake for the asker or its successor, or ruling-only just records. Answers bound for one thread are batched into a single wake
build_surface: bb thread spawn for briefs; Aleph wake mechanics (mk-a4o0.x) for needs-context
pick-time re-check of hash and preconditions (new)

steps.step: Home writes the ruling as a signed file — the ratification block plus bead, asking thread, options shown, continuation and state — into the project's docs/decisions/ or the Uqbar, and closes the bead
build_surface: ruling file writer + ssh-keygen -Y sign with Home's key (new)

steps.step: On its next turn the asking thread, or whichever thread now works that project, sees one line saying what was ruled and what ran — without a wake spent to tell it
build_surface: Clavain UserPromptSubmit ruling feed hook with per-project cache (new)

steps.step: The continuation's outcome comes back to the rail: the command's exit, the brief's result, or the asker's follow-up. A failure keeps the ruling but sets its state to failed and reopens a decision owed on the rail: retry, pick another option, or hand it to a thread
build_surface: continuation outcome on the ruling's state field (new)

mental_model: Decisions leak out of the estate when they are buried in chat, and they cost the most when answering them wakes a big context just to hear 'option 2'. mk asked for 'the most token efficient approach' and accepted building something new for it: the asker says in advance what each answer should cause, so the answer itself does the work. A pick is an approval, not a message — 'Everything on pick' — so what the option shows is exactly what runs. A decision is owed until it is ruled; once ruled it is a file Home signed on mk's pick, and a ruling an agent writes by hand shows as proposed.

closed_decisions: A decision owed is a hub-tracker bead; answering closes it and writes a ruling file (one-place brainstorm decisions 3 and 9)

Each option carries one continuation: a command (zero tokens), a brief (fresh small thread), needs-context (wakes the asker or its successor), or ruling-only (records the ruling; the feed tells the thread). Answers to one thread are batched (decision 13; ruling-only added by mk 2026-09-24 at validation)

Every continuation command runs on mk's pick; the option shows the exact command and the command is frozen by hash when filed. This amends the attention-map ruling that approval weight scales with blast radius (decision 14)
A ruling is a Markdown file carrying the ratification block plus bead, asking_thread, options_shown, continuation and state, signed by Home; unsigned files render as proposed (decision 16)
Decisions are fire-and-forget; the thread learns the answer from the ruling feed, not from a wake, unless it chose needs-context (decision 17)
Project rulings go in that project's docs/decisions/; estate-wide rulings go in the Uqbar (decision 12)

closed_decisions.decision: Stale decisions get both guards: Home marks them stale on the rail, and every pick re-checks the continuation's hash and preconditions, turning into a re-ask if they fail. mk 2026-09-24 at validation
A failed continuation reopens as a decision owed: the ruling stands with state failed, and the rail offers retry, another option, or a hand-off to a thread. One queue. mk 2026-09-24 at validation

Home signs with its own dedicated ed25519 key on the host that runs Aleph (zklw), used for nothing else. Its public key sits in an allowed_signers file committed to the Uqbar, so every machine learns it through git; rotation adds the new key with valid-after and expires the old. mk 2026-09-24 at validation

The filing helper requires a continuation kind on every option; ruling-only is the explicit kind for 'just record it'. Agents learn from the helper's prompts and worked examples in the Clavain guidance. mk 2026-09-24 at validation

Home's key accepts the same-user risk: agents on zklw run as mk and could reach the key, as with Claude Code and Codex, where the sandbox is the boundary. The key stops hand-written rulings, not a hostile agent. mk 2026-09-25 after flux-drive
An option is needs-context unless the asker explicitly gives a command; a wrong-kind command fails and reopens as owed. mk 2026-09-25 (brainstorm decision 22)
A command option may carry a revert command, frozen by the same hash; the ruling card offers revert, which runs it and reopens the decision. mk 2026-09-25 (decision 22)
v1 ships command, needs-context and ruling-only; the brief kind returns if the trial shows many decisions waking large askers. mk 2026-09-25 (decision 22)

A pick runs once: the ruling is written as running before the command starts, and after a crash it reopens as owed, marked interrupted, never re-run. The hash freezes command, cwd, an env allowlist and called-script hashes. mk 2026-09-25 (decision 21)
The feed carries only the picked option label and outcome state, never the asker's free text. mk 2026-09-25 (decision 21)

implied_features.feature: Clavain decision-filing helper and agent guidance
Decision bead fields: options, recommendation, continuations, command hash, asking thread
Home rail and decision card in the Aleph plugin
Continuation runner, brief spawner and batched needs-context wakes in autarch serve
Signed ruling file writer (project docs/decisions/ and Uqbar)

reference_lineage.what_it_shaped: The negative space: a card that expires after 30 minutes, one open at a time, and needs the thread alive. Decisions here outlive the thread and do not hold it open
The ratification block the ruling file reuses, and the rule that only mk moves a fact to ruled

evidence.quote: what is the most token efficient approach? it's okay if we need to build something new
evidence.assumption_tested: That delivering the answer to the asker is the natural design — the cost is the context that wakes to act on it
That high-blast-radius continuations need a second approval step

evidence.quote: all of these, but primarily 4 and 2
evidence.assumption_tested: Which attention leaks matter — decisions owed is one of the two primary leaks
That the decide-and-continue journey, as drafted, is how mk wants decisions to work

success_condition: mk answers a morning's worth of decisions from Home in a few minutes, never opening the asking threads, and each pick visibly lands — the command ran, the brief started, the asker knew on its next turn — so they recognize decisions as something they direct from one place, not something they chase through chat.

Softened 'no agent can make one look ruled' to match the accepted same-user risk (brainstorm decision 21)
Recorded mk's rulings on decisions 21 and 22: needs-context default, revert command, brief deferred past v1, pick-once, hash scope, feed fields
